aws-redshift-s3:position-deletes:v2.notes: Measured on Redshift Serverless 1.0.416217 (S3 Tables mode): a DELETE writes position delete files and leaves the data files in place, confirmed from the Iceberg snapshot summary (delete-files=1, total-position-deletes=1, data files unchanged). caveats: v3 tables record deletes as deletion vectors instead; a v3 table cannot add new positional delete files, though it can still read existing ones

aws-redshift-s3:position-deletes:v3.notes: Measured on Redshift Serverless 1.0.416217 (S3 Tables mode): Format-version 3 is not reachable through Redshift on S3 Tables: a CREATE TABLE requesting 'format-version'='3' is accepted without error and the stored table is format-version 2 (confirmed with SHOW TABLE), the same way PARTITIONED BY is accepted at CREATE and silently discarded. Redshift itself supports v3 -- see the S3 buckets mode.

aws-redshift-s3:equality-deletes:v2.notes: Not supported as a write operation. Redshift's own writer produces position deletes, not equality deletes -- a measured DELETE reported total-equality-deletes=0 alongside total-position-deletes=1. It can read equality delete files written by another engine, but that read half is not verified by this suite: no engine in the harness writes equality delete files (Spark's DELETE either writes positional deletes or rewrites whole data files), so no fixture carrying equality deletes can be built. A Flink upsert sink with equality fields would be needed.

aws-redshift-s3:polaris:v2.notes: Reachable read-only through AWS Glue catalog federation, not natively. Apache Polaris (including Snowflake Polaris) is federated into the Glue Data Catalog as a federated Iceberg catalog, and Redshift queries the resulting tables through a Glue database resource link (external schema or the automounted awsdatacatalog), with Lake Formation vending scoped credentials. Redshift still has no Iceberg REST client of its own -- the Data Catalog speaks Iceberg REST to the remote catalog on its behalf -- so this is a query path over federation rather than native catalog support.
caveats: Reached indirectly: the remote catalog is federated into the Glue Data Catalog, and Redshift queries it through a Glue database resource link, not by speaking Iceberg REST itself
Read path only. Access is granted as Lake Formation SELECT/DESCRIBE on the federated tables; creating or writing tables in the remote catalog from Redshift is not part of this

Requires Lake Formation to register the federation and vend scoped credentials; external schemas additionally require catalog, compute and S3 bucket in the same Region (automount handles cross-Region)
Not verified by this suite: no federated remote catalog is configured in the test account

Redshift itself supports v3 -- see the S3 buckets mode.
